---
title: "AIPW (Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting)"
---

Use the [synthetic data setup](index.qmd#synthetic-example-data) first; it defines
`data` and the columns used below. These are advanced direct R examples.

Combine outcome and propensity models, with optional cross-fitting. Double
robustness still requires the other identification and regularity assumptions.
For binary outcomes, the current estimator reports risk differences, not ORs.

```r
aipw_result <- causal_aipw(data, "Immunotherapy", "Response",
                           confounders = c("Age", "Sex", "Stage", "ECOG"),
                           outcome_type = "binary",
                           crossfit = TRUE,  # Cross-fitting to reduce overfitting
                           K = 5)
```

## Read the result

For non-survival outcomes, current outputs are RiskDiff or MeanDiff. Cross-fitting does not remove the identification assumptions. Continuous-exposure policies and survival contrasts need explicit eligible settings; the simple binary-exposure example does not establish their validation.

See [effect scales and reporting](../results/reading-results.qmd),
[diagnostics](../results/diagnostics.qmd) and the
[current support reference](../reference/validation.qmd).
